SCENE CONTEXT
A coastal city seen from high ground inland, still and empty in the morning. A wave crosses the horizon, takes the waterfront, and keeps moving inland until the city is gone beneath it.

LOCATION MAP
Foreground: the dark scrub and rock of a hillside ridge crossing the bottom of frame, out of focus. Midground: the city on the coastal plain below, a dense grid of low buildings running out to a cluster of tall towers along the seafront, arterial roads cutting through it, everything compressed flat by the long lens. Background: the open ocean beyond the shoreline, filling the upper third of frame, and a flat pale horizon above it. The camera is elevated on the ridge, looking down and out toward the sea. Sunlight comes from high SCREEN-LEFT and behind the camera. All movement in this shot travels from the horizon toward the camera, from the top of frame downward.
Operator anchored on the shadow side of the ridge, on the axis between the high ground and the seafront towers.

FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
Frame one is ordinary and completely still: the city laid out below in flat morning light, tower blocks catching the sun along the seafront, the ocean calm beyond them, the horizon a clean flat line. Nothing moves — no traffic, no people, no birds. A thin haze sits over the grid at 20% density. The city occupies the lower two thirds of frame, the ocean and horizon the upper third.

FORMAT MODE
One continuous shot, 8 seconds, real time throughout. The camera does not cut on its own.

OPTICS
EWS, 12° FOV, extreme telephoto compression flattening the ridge, the city and the ocean into stacked planes with almost no perspective falloff. Deep focus holding the city and the horizon critically sharp with the foreground scrub soft. Rectilinear prime character, genuine photographic motion blur at a true 180-degree shutter. No focal drift.

CAMERA
Locked off and heavy on a tripod, completely static, carrying only a faint organic tremor of real operator breath. From 4.5s a low structural vibration comes up through the ground into the frame, a fast fine shudder that builds. The camera holds its exact framing for the entire shot — it never pans, tilts, zooms, racks or moves to follow anything. Tonal character of a wide-latitude cinema sensor: the sunlit white water rolls off gently into highlight without clipping, and the shadowed streets hold detail.

ACTION
0.0s to 1.8s — the city sits still and empty in flat morning light. The ocean beyond is calm with slow surface texture. Nothing moves anywhere in frame.
1.8s to 3.0s — the horizon thickens. A dark band builds along it and grows upward, resolving into a wall of water advancing toward the shore, its crest breaking white along its full width. It stands as tall as the seafront towers and keeps growing as it comes.
3.0s to 4.5s — it reaches the shoreline at 90 km/h and takes the waterfront. The seafront towers disappear into it one row at a time from the front, each one swallowed whole rather than falling — visible one moment, gone under white the next. Brown-grey sediment blooms along the base of the front where it tears across the shallows.
4.5s to 6.5s — the front pushes inland through the city grid, its leading edge running fastest along the wide arterial roads so it advances in fingers ahead of itself, low buildings going under in blocks behind it. Dust and debris lift off the leading edge and hang above it in a dirty haze. The city disappears from the top of frame downward, row by row.
6.5s to 8.0s — most of the grid is gone. What is left of the city is a scatter of rooftops and tower tops standing out of a continuous moving sheet of brown-white water. The front is still advancing toward the camera when the shot ends, the high ground in the foreground still dry.
The camera holds still throughout; all movement is the water, the debris and the dust.

PHYSICS
An enormous real water mass with genuine inertia, travelling in one consistent direction for the entire shot, from the horizon toward the camera. It advances steadily and continuously and never surges, retreats, oscillates or curls back on itself. The leading edge is irregular and follows the real ground beneath it — running fast down wide roads and open ground, slowing where dense blocks resist it — so the front is always ragged and fingered rather than a straight line. Water goes white and aerated where it breaks over structures, and lifts brown-grey suspended sediment and debris that spreads and trails behind the front in real plumes. Buildings are submerged rather than demolished: they disappear beneath the surface with their shapes visible for a moment as shadow under shallow water, then gone as depth swallows them. Dust and light debris lift off the leading edge and drift upward under real air resistance. The ground and the terrain stay exactly where they are — hills, ridges and the coastal plain keep their shape and elevation, and only the water moves.

LIGHTING
Sunlight only, from high SCREEN-LEFT and behind the camera, fixed at 5600K and completely unchanged for all eight seconds. Flat direct morning light on the city with short hard shadows from the towers. The advancing white water catches the sun and becomes the brightest thing in frame, holding that brightness as it comes. Haze sits at 20% over the city at the start and thickens to 45% as dust lifts off the front. The light does not change, dim, flare or shift colour at any point.

COLOR GRADE
Opening roughly 45% pale grey-brown from the city grid and its concrete, 30% flat blue from the ocean and sky, 15% dark green from the hillside scrub, 10% white from sunlit tower faces. Across the shot the white and brown climb hard as the water arrives, ending near 50% aerated white, 30% brown-grey sediment, 15% remaining grey rooftops and 5% dark green foreground. Blacks sit lifted, never crushed. Colour comes from the water, the concrete and the sediment under plain daylight — natural, documentary, unstylised.

AUDIO
Diegetic only. Opening on near-silence: a faint wind across the ridge and the flat quiet of a city with nothing moving in it. From 1.8s a low distant roar arrives and builds steadily, deepening and broadening as the front nears, the sound of an enormous mass of water in motion. Under it from 4.5s a deep ground rumble transmitted through the hillside, felt more than heard. Structural sounds carry thinly across the distance — concrete grinding, glass going, long low collapses — all of it delayed and softened by the range. No voice, no scream, no siren. No music, no score, no soundtrack, no underscore, no ambient pad, no drone, no tone bed, no swell, no sting.

STYLE
Ultra-photoreal cinematic capture, 8K, fine organic 65mm film grain and halation, high dynamic range holding detail in both the sunlit white water and the shadowed streets, grounded documentary realism as though shot on a long lens from a real hillside.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
Real time throughout, 24fps. No on-screen text, captions, subtitles, watermarks, logos or overlays anywhere in frame.

POSITIVE LOCKS
One continuous shot with no cuts. The camera stays completely locked off in the same framing for all eight seconds and never pans, tilts, zooms or follows. The city is empty and still from the first frame — no people, no vehicles, no movement of any kind before the water arrives, and no person appears anywhere in frame at any point. The water travels in one single direction throughout, from the horizon toward the camera, and advances steadily without surging or retreating. Buildings go under the surface and disappear rather than exploding, toppling or breaking apart. The front stays ragged and fingered, running ahead down roads and open ground. The terrain and ground elevation stay fixed and only the water moves. The water is still advancing at the final frame with the foreground high ground still dry. Sunlight stays fixed from high SCREEN-LEFT at a constant angle and intensity, with no flash, no darkening and no colour shift. Natural daylight colour throughout with no glow, no fire and no coloured light of any kind.
